cells.tense: You're tending it right now, and you know it — pen in hand, no bracing.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the long middle of the work, where holding on and letting go are the same motion
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've finished to the person it was for — let it be received, not just done. When this is in balance, the letting go comes as its own kind of completion, release that feels like arrival rather than loss.
cells.core: You're the one tending what's growing, and you've got the two hard things held at once — what needs to stay and what needs to be let go — without forcing either one. That's not a small trick. Most people pick one demand and drop the other; you're keeping both alive with the same pair of hands, and it shows in what's coming up around you. The care you're spending isn't burning you out. It's just working.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what grows and holding both demands at once.

cells.tense: You're leaning into a season that hasn't arrived yet, holding the shape of it before it's yours to hold.
cells.verb: tending and managing ahead of what's actually growing
cells.place: out past the edge of what you can actually carry today
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're holding for later and set it down until it's actually here — imagination fed by what's already happened, not by what you're bracing for. When this comes back to balance, the care stops costing you more than it gives; you can hold the space without gripping it.
cells.core: You've started carrying things before they're yours to carry. Loads nobody handed you yet, seasons that haven't arrived, outcomes you're already steeling against — and the bracing is eating the energy that was supposed to go into the tending. You know what's coming so well that you've stopped being where you are. The holding is real; the trouble is you're holding forward, and the present doesn't get the part of you that knows how to do this.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying loads that haven't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you, and your hands are still remembering the handle.
cells.verb: tending what grew and not reaching for what's next
cells.place: back at the point where the carrying went past what you had, and something in you set the load down for good
cells.ask: Let one thing you already grew shine on its own — tell someone what it turned into, without asking anything back. Strength comes back from continued hoping, not from re-gripping what's finished. When the balance returns, the care stops draining you; you're making room instead of just holding the line.
cells.core: You're strong and you're not spending it. Somewhere behind you, the carrying went past what you had and something in you decided tending wasn't worth the cost — so the strength stayed, and the reaching stopped. What you grew already grew; you're just not standing in front of it anymore. The capacity didn't disappear. The hand that said yes to the next thing did.
cells.sheetLine: You were strong enough to tend it and you stopped reaching for the next thing.

cells.tense: Your hands are already tending it — you just haven't looked up to see whose work this is.
cells.verb: tending what grows as if it were tending itself
cells.place: inside a job you're already doing while calling it just the way things run
cells.ask: Say plainly, once, that this is you doing it — let the work you've done be seen and named by the person it was for. When this is in balance, the finishing feels like release instead of something unfinished; the sacrifice gets honored and the honoring completes it.
cells.core: You're doing the tending right now — the holding, the keeping, the deciding what gets fed and what gets let go — and you talk about it like it's just what anyone would do, or like the situation is running itself. You are the one doing it. You just haven't said so. The care gets spent and the credit goes somewhere else, usually to nobody, which means something that was finished never gets to feel finished.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending this. You just haven't said so.
